description:
pkix-ct/src/log_list.rs:26-53

`CtLog` is `pub struct` with seven public fields and no
`#[non_exhaustive]`. Real-world CT log metadata that a v0.2 might
need to surface but cannot be added without a major bump:

- `operator_id` / `operator_name`: required by CA/B Forum TLS BR
  §3.2.2.9 for diversity policy ("at least two SCTs from logs
  operated by two different operators").
- `mmd_seconds`: Maximum Merge Delay; consumers checking SCT freshness
  against log-claimed MMD need it.
- `log_type`: prod vs test; tile vs RFC-6962 v1; Static-CT vs classic.
- `monitor_url` separate from `submission_url` (Argon does this).
- `temporal_interval_ms`: shard logs have a per-shard time window
  that is narrower than `usable_from..retired_at` and excludes SCTs
  outside the temporal interval as fraud.

All five are real metadata fields exposed by Chrome's
`log_list.json` v3 schema. The Google parser at
`pkix-ct/src/log_list.rs:120-228` already deserializes some of them
implicitly (via `#[serde(default)]` ignoring unknown fields) but the
`CtLog` struct cannot store them without a breaking change.

Recommendation: `#[non_exhaustive]` plus a `CtLog::builder()` or
`CtLog::new(log_id, key_der)` returning a value that callers can
update via setter methods. Direct field literals become inadmissible,
but accessor methods on `&CtLog` can stay stable.

Caller impact: every shard-aware policy check, every operator-diversity
check, and every MMD-freshness check has to wait for a major bump or
work around the absent fields by maintaining its own parallel
`log_id -> metadata` map.
title: CtLog lacks #[non_exhaustive] — adding fields like operator_id, mmd, log_type is breaking
